observations.contract: Hitbox admission and symbolic slab overflow
observations.trace: The config validator requires seven unique body parts, finite centers and finite positive half extents, with no upper bound in the selected hitbox check. Consider an otherwise valid config whose selected box has center (0,0,0) and each half extent f32::MAX, target identity Transform and attacker position (1,0,1). Lock-pinned glam normalization yields direction approximately (1/sqrt(2),0,1/sqrt(2)); each MAX/abs(direction component) is +infinity under IEEE f32, including division by zero for y. All three finite filters discard the ratios, leaving the fold at +infinity. Multiplying the direction yields local point (+infinity,NaN,+infinity).
observations.remaining: This is source and symbolic IEEE reasoning only; no configuration was written, no attack, math implementation, network codec, particle, renderer, test or product ran. Ordinary authored hitboxes use small metre values. The existence of an admitted custom-config contact is conditional on the rest of startup and combat gates; downstream acceptance/visual impact must not be assumed. Repair must preserve target-local semantics and ordinary valid boxes.
